name: Mallothi
overview: Mallothi was a male Levite distinguished as the son of Heman and chosen nineteenth by lot among the singers. He was set apart to prophesy using musical instruments such as lyres, harps, and cymbals, serving an important role in the worship practices of ancient Israel. His role highlights the Levites' special function in temple music and prophetic ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name Mallothi means 'my expression,' reflecting a personal or expressive quality. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 25:4, does not indicate a title but provides insight into his individual identity within the Levitical singers.
familyAndRelationships: Mallothi was the son of Heman, a notable figure in Israel's musical and prophetic tradition. Scripture does not record any other family relationships for Mallothi beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Mallothi's significance lies in his role as part of the Levitical singers who were divinely appointed to prophesy through music. Being chosen nineteenth by lot emphasizes the ordered and God-directed selection process for temple service. His service with lyres, harps, and cymbals illustrates the integration of music and prophecy in Israel's worship, underscoring the spiritual importance of the Levites in leading God's people.
